$comment: Where each drawing in this folder came from. node site/scripts/art.mts checks it: every file listed, checksums, licences, and the public-domain rules (Verne's own illustrators, published by 1871, from Commons or Gallica). Verne quotes follow Project Gutenberg #164, which numbers chapters differently from some editions.

art.title: The Nautilus, in profile
art.creator: Ouro HX contributors
art.modifications: None: drawn for this site from Verne's text alone. Not after any film or later design: no riveted fish tail, no dorsal fins, no saw-tooth crest. Hull length to beam about 9 to 1 (232 by 26 feet). Colours come from the theme (stage.css).

shape.quote: It is an elongated cylinder with conical ends. It is very like a cigar in shape
shape.chapter: Part One, Chapter XII, “Some Figures” (Project Gutenberg #164)

shape.quote: The length of this cylinder, from stem to stern, is exactly 232 feet, and its maximum breadth is twenty-six feet.
shape.chapter: Part One, Chapter XII, “Some Figures” (Project Gutenberg #164)

shape.quote: The platform was only three feet out of water. The front and back of the Nautilus was of that spindle-shape which caused it justly to be compared to a cigar.
shape.chapter: Part One, Chapter XIII, “The Black River” (Project Gutenberg #164)

shape.quote: I noticed that its iron plates, slightly overlaying each other, resembled the shell which clothes the bodies of our large terrestrial reptiles.
shape.chapter: Part One, Chapter XIII, “The Black River” (Project Gutenberg #164)

shape.quote: Toward the middle of the platform the long-boat, half buried in the hull of the vessel, formed a slight excrescence.
shape.chapter: Part One, Chapter XIII, “The Black River” (Project Gutenberg #164)

shape.quote: Fore and aft rose two cages of medium height with inclined sides, and partly closed by thick lenticular glasses; one destined for the steersman who directed the Nautilus, the other containing a brilliant lantern to give light on the road.
shape.chapter: Part One, Chapter XIII, “The Black River” (Project Gutenberg #164)

shape.quote: Behind the steersman’s cage is placed a powerful electric reflector, the rays from which light up the sea for half a mile in front.
shape.chapter: Part One, Chapter XII, “Some Figures” (Project Gutenberg #164)

shape.quote: I use an ordinary rudder fixed on the back of the stern-post … by means of two inclined planes fastened to its sides, opposite the centre of flotation
shape.chapter: Part One, Chapter XII, “Some Figures” (Project Gutenberg #164)

shape.quote: The Nautilus, by the action of its screw, slid down the inclined planes and buried itself in the lowest depths of the sea.
shape.chapter: Part Two, Chapter VII, “The Mediterranean in Forty-eight Hours” (Project Gutenberg #164)

shape.quote: It is armed with a steel spur as good as Master Land’s harpoon, I imagine.
shape.chapter: Part Two, Chapter XII, “Cachalots and Whales” (Project Gutenberg #164)
